.wealthoracle.co.uk/company-results Baltic Classifieds delivered a workmanlike full year to 30 April 2026, with revenue up 7% to €88.5m and adjusted basic EPS rising 9% to 12.3 euro cent, while statutory basic EPS jumped 16% to 10.8 euro cent as amortisation of acquired intangibles rolled off. The EBITDA margin held steady at an enviable 78%, and cash conversion remained at 99%, underscoring the durability of the Baltic classifieds franchise even as the Estonian vehicle tax and an unusually severe winter suppressed C2C auto listing volumes by 26%. Real Estate was the standout, growing 17% on the back of 20% B2C and 12% C2C gains, while Jobs & Services accelerated into the second half to finish up 9%; Auto was flat but resilient given the headwinds. The more striking story is capital allocation: BCG returned €101.1m to shareholders via buybacks and dividends, repurchasing 10% of issued share capital and drawing €73m of a new €125m SEB facility, with leverage stepping up from 0.1x to 0.7x — a deliberate signal that the Board views the share price as undervaluing the model amid market anxiety over AI disruption. A final ordinary dividend of 2.8 euro cent plus a 0.3 euro cent special takes total dividends to 4.4 euro cent, up 16%. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of around 10%, second-half weighted, with margins staying in the mid-70s — a credible reacceleration underpinned by C2C repricing already implemented in March. .wealthoracle.co.uk/company-results
